AUSTRALIAN LAWYER NAMED DUTERTE’S ASSOCIATE COUNSEL AT ICC

Australian lawyer Kate Gibson has been appointed as new associate counsel of former president Rodrigo Duterte at the International Criminal Court (ICC). 

Gibson, who has appeared in various international courts and tribunals, was tapped by Duterte’s lead defense counsel Peter Haynes to be part of the defense team, according to an ICC Registry filing released on Tuesday. 

She formally accepted the role on May 18, 2026.

Gibson worked with Haynes on the ICC case against Congolese politician Jean-Pierre Bemba, who was acquitted on appeal in 2018.

She was also appointed as associate counsel to represent the interests of Ugandan militant Joseph Kony during his confirmation hearings, which were held in absentia last year. 

A former president of the Association of Defence Counsel Practising Before the International Courts and Tribunals, Gibson also appeared before other international tribunals, including the Special Court for Sierra Leone, UN Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals, UN International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers. 

Gibson served as legal consultant to the International Fact-Finding Mission on Myanmar and currently represents some Rohingya victims, according to her profile on the website of the United Kingdom-based Doughty Street Chambers, where she is an associate. | via Janvic Mateo

DILG: THERE WAS NO ATTACK ON THE SENATE

DOST-PAGASA, in partnership with the UK Met Office, is currently hosting the Weather and Climate Science for Service Partnership – Southeast Asia (WCSSP SeA) Regional Workshop from May 18–21, 2026, in Mactan, Cebu.

This year’s theme, “A Decade of Collaboration in Weather and Climate: From Scientific Innovations to Effective and Actionable Forecast Applications,” highlights ten years of partnership among countries in Southeast Asia and the UK Met Office in advancing the understanding of large-scale and convective-scale weather and climate science. It also emphasizes the importance of translating scientific advancements into effective warnings, forecasts, and actionable advice for communities and decision-makers.

The workshop likewise aims to discuss future plans for ongoing projects within the Southeast Asian region and identify opportunities for collaboration with other potential partners. This partnership further demonstrates the role of DOST-PAGASA as one of the region’s leading institutions in promoting the advancement of weather and climate services.
